scenarios.label: Background Radiation Scenario (GCR Dominated)
scenarios.radiationSource: Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR: ~85–90% protons, ~10–14% alpha particles, ~1% HZE ions + secondary neutrons/gammas)
scenarios.referenceOrigin: NASA PDS MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0 · Curiosity RAD at Gale Crater (Sols 13–4550 & pre-event Sols 1809–1811)
scenarios.shelterAdvisory: Nominal galactic cosmic ray background. High-energy GCR ions penetrate thin EVA suits and shallow regolith overhangs; cumulative EVA exposure is governed primarily by total mission duration.
limitations: Measured by Curiosity RAD in Gale Crater (~-4.5 km MOLA), not in-situ at Jezero Crater (~-2.5 km MOLA).
Jezero's ~2 km higher elevation reduces overlying CO2 mass column by ~15-18%, which can increase surface GCR dose rate within the +/-22% uncertainty band.
Absorbed dose (uGy) is a physical energy deposition quantity and must not be equated 1:1 with biological dose equivalent (uSv).

scenarios.label: Historical Solar Particle Event Scenario (Sep 2017 GLE 72)
scenarios.radiationSource: GCR Background + Solar Energetic Particles (SEP protons >100 MeV penetrating Mars CO2 atmosphere during GLE 72)
scenarios.referenceOrigin: NASA PDS MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0 (Sols 1811–1815) & MAVEN SEP Orbital Context (Zeitlin et al., 2018)
scenarios.shelterAdvisory: Historical SEP surge scenario (modeled on the Sept 10–13, 2017 GLE 72 event where surface dose rate rose ~2.3x above GCR background to 25.89 uGy/h). Pre-mission planning advisory: minimize exposed target stay duration, keep return margin positive, and note high-obstruction scarp alcoves along the traverse.
limitations: Historical reference event (September 2017 GLE 72); this system does NOT predict the timing or intensity of future solar particle events.
More extreme historical SPEs (e.g., Carrington 1859, August 1972, October 1989) with harder proton spectra could produce substantially higher surface dose rates than Sept 2017.
MAVEN SEP measures orbital particle fluxes above the atmosphere; surface dose rates here come from MSL-RAD surface measurements underneath ~20-23 g/cm² of CO2.
